title: How Dagobert Renouf sold logo spots on his wedding suit and landed a sales job
summary: Dagobert Renouf, a bootstrapped founder short on cash, asked his audience for help paying for his wedding and turned their joke into a stunt: selling logo spots on his suit to fellow entrepreneurs for about 10,000 euros. The stunt shows how to use a community, persistence and quality execution, and it led to an unexpected sales job.

principles.text: Build in public and ask your audience openly; the best idea can come back from the community.
principles.quote: I posted something like, "I have to find a way to pay for my wedding. No idea how I'm going to do it."

principles.text: Get out of your comfort zone and try crazy ideas if you want to make it as an entrepreneur.
principles.quote: You've got to get out of your comfort zone. You try crazy shit if you want to make it.

principles.text: Connect an unusual idea to what the people involved care about to bring them on board.
principles.quote: What made her come around, and what was making this whole thing beautiful, was when I really connected it to the fact that it was a way to bring my community to our wedding.

principles.text: Great ideas look crazy first and obvious later, so keep pushing through months of public skepticism.
principles.quote: At first, they think you're crazy, and then it seems obvious.

principles.text: Execution quality matters: make a sponsored stunt look premium so it reads as credible, not as a joke.
principles.quote: Once I started doing the suit, then I'm like, "OK, now I want it to look good. I don't want to look like an idiot."

principles.text: Visibility around a bold public idea attracts unexpected opportunities, like a job offer from someone who kept engaging.
principles.quote: Without the suit, I would have never gotten this job.
